messages.text: How do changes in radar technology affect the measurement capability required from Signaling / Non-signaling Tester?

Short answer: as wireless technology moves to newer standards, wider bandwidths, higher frequencies, multi-channel/MIMO operation, and cellular/non-cellular coexistence, testers need broader technology coverage, more RF chains/ports, wider measurement bandwidth, and more realistic signaling or non-signaling RF measurement modes [19][21][24].
| Technology change | Measurement capability impact | Signaling tester implication | Non-signaling tester implication |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wi‑Fi 7 / IEEE 802.11be alongside LTE and 5G creates new parallel-operation test challenges.[19] | Tester must cover both cellular and non-cellular standards in one setup.[19] | CMX500 is positioned as a multi-technology, multi-channel signaling tester with integrated Wi‑Fi 7 functionality for cellular and non-cellular testing.[19] | CMP180 is positioned for production non-signaling RF testing across cellular and non-cellular technologies including Wi‑Fi 6E, Wi‑Fi 7, and 5G NR FR1.[24] |
| Wi‑Fi 7 R&D requires signaling-mode testing under real-world conditions, including RF TX/RX characteristics, MLO, multiple RF chains, 2x2 MIMO, 6 GHz out-of-band discovery, coexistence, and E2E capabilities.[21] | Measurement must handle multiple RF chains, MIMO, coexistence, and end-to-end behavior rather than only isolated RF parameters.[21] | Signaling testers need network/device interaction plus RF TX/RX measurement in realistic operating modes.[21] | Not the primary R&D mode here; production focuses on fast RF measurements in non-signaling mode.[24] |
| Production WLAN RF measurements are performed in non-signaling mode to save time.[24] | Tester must provide fast RF analyzer/generator capability without establishing full protocol signaling.[24] | Signaling tester is less suited to the production-time-saving role described here.[24] | CMP180 is optimized for this non-signaling production purpose.[24] |
| Wider bandwidth is emerging beyond Wi‑Fi 7: CMP180 demonstrates a 480 MHz WLAN waveform, while Wi‑Fi 8 / IEEE 802.11bn is still not formally defined in this source.[24] | Non-signaling testers need wider analysis/generation bandwidth headroom; CMP180 is stated to support bandwidths up to 500 MHz.[24] | Signaling passages do not state a 480 MHz Wi‑Fi signaling requirement. | Non-signaling testers should support wideband waveform generation/analysis such as 480 MHz loopback verification and up to 500 MHz bandwidth.[24] |
| EMC and SAR contexts require device operation under controlled radio states or extreme transmit conditions.[3][13] | Tester must provide signaling/network-emulation functions to drive the DUT into required operating conditions.[3][13] | 5G NR SAR testing requires a 5G NR network emulator to drive the EUT to extreme transmission conditions, and EMC tests need enabled/disabled radio conditions, implying a 5G NR signaling solution.[3][13] | Non-signaling testers are not described as fulfilling these SAR/EMC signaling-control needs in the cited passages. |
【推論】For signaling testers, technology change mainly increases the need for multi-technology network emulation plus realistic RF TX/RX, MLO, MIMO, coexistence, FR1/FR2, and application/E2E coverage, because the cited CMX500 use cases combine cellular/non-cellular signaling, Wi‑Fi 7 R&D, and NR FR1/FR2 support.[1][6][19][21]
【推論】For non-signaling testers, technology change mainly increases the need for faster production RF measurements, wider bandwidth, more analyzers/generators, more RF ports, and scalable MIMO support, because the cited CMP180 role emphasizes non-signaling production testing, up to 500 MHz bandwidth, 480 MHz WLAN waveform loopback, 2x2 MIMO in one box, and 4x4 MIMO by combining two units.[24]
【推論】If the question meant “radar” literally, the knowledge base does not state radar-specific signaling or non-signaling tester requirements; the supported conclusions above apply only to wireless radio technologies such as Wi‑Fi, LTE, and 5G NR.[19][21][24]
